LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.9: Guided Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: where one is going (e.g. 你去 哪儿 Nǐ qù nǎr?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Guided Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where one is going (e.g. 你去 哪儿 Nǐ qù nǎr?
2. What strategies can you use to read texts clearly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary in varied reading contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
